section_summary.extract_value: This section, titled '1.1. The present study', outlines the aim of the current research to explore relationships between multidimensional interoceptive awareness (using the MAIA) and various positive body image facets, including body appreciation, body pride, and functionality appreciation, as well as overweight preoccupation and appearance orientation. It details specific hypotheses regarding how different MAIA subscales might relate to these body image variables. The study also aims to address limitations of previous literature by recruiting a large, diverse sample of British women and men from community samples, accounting for sex, age, and BMI.
section_summary.evidence_source: The aim of the present study was to expand the available literature considering relationships between body image and interoception by exploring the explanatory power of multidimensional IA. We were particularly keen to explore how the eight dimensions of the MAIA might be related to facets of positive body image, given the paucity of research investigating relationships between interoception and positive body image more generally. As a final aim, we sought to address these limitations in the present study by recruiting a large sample of British women and men, with a wide age range that would be more representative of age variations in community samples.
